1	# External documentation and project review — 2026-07-12
2	
3	- Status: Advisory research record
4	- Input: External review supplied by the repository owner
5	- Scope: Complete document set, project direction, quality process, release readiness, and continuity
6	  evidence strategy
7	- Not equivalent to: Independent post-fix code/security GO, statistical continuity evidence, or npm
8	  publication approval
9	
10	## Independently checked baseline
11	
12	The reviewer reported reading the complete document set and independently checking:
13	
14	- package identity `carrylog@0.1.0-beta.5`;
15	- clean `validate --json` output;
16	- actual completion of the 157-test suite.
17	
18	The review found no material mismatch in the sampled documentation claims. This establishes document
19	credibility for the review but does not replace the remaining exact-commit CI or post-fix code review.
20	
21	## Strengths identified
22	
23	- strict separation between claims and executed evidence;
24	- unusually complete failure and correction history in `docs/engineering-log.md`;
25	- high-quality ADRs with rejected alternatives, consequences, validation, and supersession;
26	- immutable failed release tags and exact-artifact provenance policy;
27	- epistemically careful continuity audit definitions and threats to validity;
28	- productive dogfood that found executable-resolution and sandbox-stderr defects.
29	
30	These strengths are retained. They are not treated as evidence of user demand.
31	
32	## Material findings
33	
34	### Product and delivery risk outranks further defensive breadth
35	
36	The project has strong integrity controls but no unscoped npm publication, no external adoption story,
37	and only one authenticated Claude reconstruction. Future work should prioritize installability, a
38	short successful workflow, and external outcome evidence.
39	
40	### The original audit protocol was too large as a first step
41	
42	The draft requested a comprehensive factorial program without a funded reviewer or established user
43	base. A small preregistered maintainer pilot should precede an independent larger evaluation.
44	
45	### Research constraints needed an accepted decision
46	
47	The prohibition on conversation-resume, arbitrary-switch, retention-value, and compact-superiority
48	claims should not depend on a disposable draft.
49	
50	### README optimized for auditors rather than new users
51	
52	The initial value, before/after workflow, real output, and usable current installation path were not
53	prominent. Registry commands preceded the fact that the package does not exist.
54	
55	### Volatile evidence was copied across documents
56	
57	Exact test counts, coverage, package size, run IDs, and publication failure details appeared in
58	multiple manually maintained files, recreating the drift problem Carrylog is intended to reduce.
59	
60	### Documentation freshness was implicit
61	
62	Historical logs, rolling status, user docs, policies, and compatibility references lacked one
63	documented ownership and refresh model.
64	
65	### User outcomes were not part of executed quality evidence
66	
67	Technical gates were comprehensive, but product-scope outcomes such as reduced re-explanation or
68	repeated work had not been measured.
69	
70	## Disposition
71	
72	| Recommendation | Disposition | Rationale or action |
73	| --- | --- | --- |
74	| Recover first npm publication | Accepted, externally blocked | Registry still returns `E404`; the protected `NPM_TOKEN` exists but failed package creation and must be replaced by the owner without sharing it in chat or local files. |
75	| Rewrite README value-first | Accepted | Source workflow, value statement, before/after, human output, and abbreviated JSON shape now precede detailed contracts. |
76	| Run a minimum Tier 1 pilot | Accepted | ADR-0012 and `tier1-pilot-protocol.md` define two repositories, five tasks, three conditions, and two harnesses. |
77	| Promote interim constraints to ADR | Accepted | ADR-0012 is accepted and indexed. |
78	| Pull external adoption forward | Accepted | Roadmap now places adoption and outcome measurement before 0.2 expansion. |
79	| Single-source volatile evidence | Accepted | `docs/documentation-policy.md` assigns current and historical evidence ownership. |
80	| Add freshness contracts | Accepted | The documentation policy defines review cadence by document class. |
81	| Centralize performance budgets | Accepted | `docs/testing-strategy.md` now lists implementation budgets in one table. |
82	| Position as repository memory governance | Accepted | Current claims remain checkpoint/project-memory governance, not universal conversation resume. |
83	| Add issue templates immediately | Deferred | Useful after publication and contributor traffic; not the current blocker. |
84	| Add an asciinema demo immediately | Deferred | A real recording is valuable only after the executable installation path exists; textual output is added now. |
85	| Revert or de-prioritize existing ctime/security fixes | Rejected retrospectively | The high-severity issue was independently reproduced and cheaply fixed with regression coverage. Future prioritization changes, but validated integrity is not removed. |
86	| Release automatically after a fixed number of days | Qualified | Research gaps may become documented limitations, but integrity, data-loss, package, and release-authenticity blockers do not expire on a calendar. |
87	| Assume AGENTS.md standardization removes the niche | Not accepted without evidence | This is an ADR-0001 revisit signal to investigate through adoption, not a proven market conclusion. |
88	
89	## Resulting order of work
90	
91	1. Complete documentation reconciliation and beta.5 local gates.
92	2. Obtain the required post-fix review and exact-commit CI.
93	3. Have the owner replace the protected shortest-lived npm bootstrap credential and recover immutable
94	   beta.4 publication through the documented workflow.
95	4. Verify a short install/init/checkpoint/resume path against the actual registry package.
96	5. Commit and execute the Tier 1 pilot protocol without journaling or compaction.
97	6. Dogfood on two additional repositories and publish sanitized findings.
98	7. Decide whether any journal, wrapper, or compactor is justified by observed failures and outcomes.
99	
100	## Evidence limits
101	
102	This review is one advisory assessment. Praise, prioritization, and market positioning are not treated
103	as facts merely because the implementation claims passed a spot check. All resulting changes remain
104	subject to normal diff review, quality gates, package verification, and Carrylog checkpointing.

1	# Continuity and compaction evidence audit brief
2	
3	- Status: Archived external-audit input; non-normative research record
4	- Prepared: 2026-07-12
5	- Scope: Cross-harness conversational continuity, session-record retention, and compaction value
6	- Product baseline: Unreleased Carrylog `0.1.0-beta.5` worktree
7	
8	## Purpose
9	
10	This brief asks an external reviewer to challenge whether Carrylog has demonstrated useful continuity
11	across Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, or future harnesses. It also asks whether retaining
12	observable conversation records or offering Carrylog-controlled compaction would create measurable
13	value rather than cost, privacy exposure, false confidence, or a second compaction failure mode.
14	
15	The document is intentionally skeptical. It does not treat file discovery, prompt injection, an
16	agent's acknowledgement, or one successful reconstruction as proof that another harness received and
17	used the same effective context. It does not assume that retaining all records is desirable, that a
18	portable compacted representation is possible, or that a Carrylog compactor would outperform a
19	harness-native compactor.
20	
21	No raw provider transcript, hidden reasoning, credential, or private session-store content is
22	included. The conversation record below contains selected user-visible statements and a reviewable
23	summary of proposals made during the design discussion.
24	
25	## Existing project claims and boundaries
26	
27	The audit must read these sources before evaluating new continuity or compaction claims:
28	
29	| Source | Relevant existing position |
30	| --- | --- |
31	| `README.md` | Carrylog shares reviewed project state, not provider-native session replay. |
32	| `docs/product-scope.md` | The current product preserves durable project truth and explicitly excludes full conversation and internal compaction reconstruction. |
33	| `docs/decisions/0001-local-first-context-compiler.md` | Repository Markdown is canonical; adapters are concise routers; agents following references remains a known dependency. |
34	| `docs/decisions/0009-configuration-v2-and-universal-surfaces.md` | Codex and Cursor share `AGENTS.md`; Claude and Gemini use distinct surfaces; v2 migration is explicit. |
35	| `docs/decisions/0010-portable-checkpoint-and-resume-boundary.md` | Continuity currently means a reviewed checkpoint plus fresh Git observation, not conversation replay or control of native compaction. |
36	| `docs/adapter-compatibility.md` | Discovery guarantees and live-conformance gaps differ by harness. |
37	| `docs/architecture.md` | The runtime is deterministic and offline; semantic freshness and authenticated launch are known gaps. |
38	| `docs/testing-strategy.md` | Tests cover structural and package contracts, while external outcome studies and complete authenticated harness coverage remain open. |
39	| `docs/threat-model.md` | Future compaction must retain recoverable history; remote, telemetry, plugin, and secret boundaries require separate review. |
40	| `ROADMAP.md` | Measured continuity is planned for 0.2; reversible compaction is planned for 0.3 and is not implemented. |
41	| `docs/engineering-log.md` | Records actual dogfood, review findings, package checks, and incomplete harness authentication. |
42	| `.agent-context/handoff.md` | Records the current beta.5 implementation evidence and unresolved review/CI risks. |
43	
44	If a statement in this brief conflicts with an accepted ADR or executable behavior, the conflict must
45	be reported rather than silently resolving it in favor of this draft.
46	
47	## Current evidence, without extrapolation
48	
49	The current worktree provides evidence for these narrow statements:
50	
51	- Carrylog can generate and validate repository instruction surfaces for Codex/Cursor, Claude Code,
52	  and Gemini CLI from one canonical configuration.
53	- `resume --json` deterministically projects reviewed checkpoint sections, always-context, an
54	  on-demand catalog, digests, and bounded Git evidence.
55	- Local Codex inspection found the generated router and generic Skill without a model call.
56	- Local Gemini inspection found the generic Skill, but an authenticated headless model response was
57	  not obtained.
58	- One authenticated Claude Code fresh session reconstructed the project, objective, next action,
59	  stale status, and risks.
60	- Cursor CLI was not installed, so no authenticated Cursor session was reconstructed.
61	- The complete local test suite and package consumers verify implementation contracts, not user-level
62	  continuity outcomes.
63	
64	The current worktree does **not** provide evidence for these broader statements:
65	
66	- that exact context bytes were delivered to every supported model invocation;
67	- that a model used delivered context rather than merely acknowledging or repeating it;
68	- that task quality is preserved after one or many same-harness or cross-harness switches;
69	- that users perceive a resumed session as a continued conversation;
70	- that retaining all observable conversation records improves outcomes;
71	- that raw history injection is preferable to a native compact, checkpoint, or selected retrieval;
72	- that a native compact produced for one harness remains valid for another harness;
73	- that a Carrylog compact is more faithful, efficient, controllable, or useful than native compact;
74	- that a universal session journal can be captured completely and safely across supported harnesses;
75	- that users always want continuity rather than a new task branch or a project-only fresh session.
76	
77	The audit must treat the second list as unproven hypotheses, not implied product behavior.
78	
79	## Conversation-derived requirements and objections
80	
81	### Initial desired outcome
82	
83	The user wants installation to reduce tool-specific setup and allow switching among Codex, Claude,
84	Cursor, and other harnesses while retaining useful context. The user also wants visible confirmation
85	that prior state was loaded, because invisible instruction discovery may not feel like a continued
86	conversation and may not demonstrate that the model used the state.
87	
88	Selected user statement:
89	
90	> 대화가 남지않는다면 사용자는 이어서 대화하는 느낌을 못 받을 수도 있어.
91	
92	The discussion separated four events that must not be conflated:
93	
94	1. a context artifact exists;
95	2. a harness includes the artifact in model input;
96	3. the model reconstructs and uses the relevant state;
97	4. the user experiences the interaction as a continuation.
98	
99	A proposed visible `continuity receipt` would report checkpoint identity, loaded sources, omissions,
100	and freshness. This is only a proposal. A receipt can prove what a wrapper attempted to deliver and
101	what the model repeated; by itself it cannot prove attention, correct use, or task continuity.
102	
103	### Record retention and destructive compaction concern
104	
105	Selected user statement:
106	
107	> carrylog설치했을 때 .gitignore에서 확인한 후 제외시키도록 하고, 여전히 걱정되는건
108	> compact를 진행하면 파괴가 되는거 아닌가?
109	
110	The discussion proposed a local ignored session journal, derived compaction artifacts, context packs,
111	and delivery receipts. It also proposed that compaction never overwrite its sources and that deletion
112	be a separate explicit operation. None of these components exists in the current product, and their
113	value, privacy model, retention defaults, completeness, storage cost, and failure behavior have not
114	been validated.
115	
116	The user questioned whether the product's purpose is indefinite retention. That question remains
117	open. Durable reviewed project state, raw observable conversation, generated compactions, and cached
118	delivery packs have different value and risk and must not inherit one retention policy by accident.
119	
120	### Evidence challenge
121	
122	Selected user statements:
123	
124	> 우선 이렇게 모든 기록을 남기는 것과 자체 compact가 주는 가치를 수치적으로 또는
125	> 수학적으로 증명해야한다.
126	
127	> 우리가 이어서 context를 얼마든지 스위치해도 그게 이어서 전달된다는 것도 증명이 되어야
128	> 한다.
129	
130	> compact가 자체 하네스가 진행했다면 그것을 계속 사용해야하지 않겠나? 그럼 compact하고
131	> 하네스를 바꾸면 그게 맥락이 이어지는게 맞나?
132	
133	> 사용자가 새로운 대화를 시작하고 싶을 수도 있다.
134	
135	> 문제를 광범위하게 다루기전에 이어서 대화조차 충분히 증명된지 의문이다.
136	
137	These objections supersede any assumption that session journaling or Carrylog compaction should move
138	directly into implementation. The next activity is evidence design and independent audit, not feature
139	construction.
140	
141	## Definitions the audit must enforce
142	
143	### Artifact continuity
144	
145	The expected files or envelope exist, are current, and have stable content identity.
146	
147	### Delivery continuity
148	
149	The exact intended context or a documented transformation of it is included in the model-visible
150	input. Instruction-file discovery alone is weaker evidence unless the harness exposes the resolved
151	prompt or another trustworthy delivery trace.
152	
153	### Reconstruction continuity
154	
155	The model can correctly recover a preregistered set of relevant facts, constraints, decisions, and
156	open work without receiving the answers in the evaluation question.
157	
158	### Behavioral continuity
159	
160	The model applies the recovered state to the next task without prohibited reversals, repeated work,
161	contradictions, or unnecessary clarification.
162	
163	### Perceived continuity
164	
165	The user understands what was and was not resumed and rates the experience as an appropriate
166	continuation. This includes the ability to reject continuity and start project-only or fully fresh
167	work.
168	
169	No single layer proves the layers below it. In particular, a receipt is not behavioral evidence, and
170	a successful task is not proof that every retained record was useful.
171	
172	## Formal measurement model
173	
174	Mathematical notation can make claims falsifiable, but it cannot prove universal product value from a
175	finite, changing set of proprietary models. The audit should require empirical estimates with
176	confidence intervals, preregistered hypotheses, and explicit limits rather than an unsupported single
177	utility score.
178	
179	For task `t`, define a preregistered relevant fact set:
180	
181	```text
182	F_t = {(f_1, w_1), ..., (f_n, w_n)}
183	```
184	
185	where `w_i` is an importance weight fixed before observing model output. Facts may include current
186	objective, protected decisions, completed verification, prohibited alternatives, known risks, and
187	the next required action.
188	
189	For a harness transition `a -> b`, measure:
190	
191	```text
192	delivery_coverage = sum(w_i * delivered_i) / sum(w_i)
193	reconstruction_recall = sum(w_i * correctly_reconstructed_i) / sum(w_i)
194	contradiction_rate = sum(w_i * contradicted_i) / sum(w_i)
195	unsupported_claim_rate = unsupported_material_claims / material_claims
196	```
197	
198	`delivered_i`, `correctly_reconstructed_i`, and `contradicted_i` are evaluator-scored indicators with
199	a written rubric. Delivery coverage is valid only when the wrapper or harness exposes sufficient
200	input evidence; otherwise it must be reported as unknown.
201	
202	Behavioral task score should be measured separately from token input, latency, monetary cost,
203	clarification count, repeated-work count, and sensitive-data exposure. A composite score with
204	arbitrary weights would hide tradeoffs. The audit should report a Pareto comparison or preregistered
205	primary and secondary outcomes.
206	
207	For `k` consecutive harness switches, define:
208	
209	```text
210	retention_k = weighted facts correctly used after switch k / total relevant fact weight
211	degradation_k = baseline_same_harness_score - switched_score_k
212	```
213	
214	The product may claim cross-harness non-inferiority only if a preregistered confidence interval for
215	the score difference stays above a justified negative margin. The margin, sample size, model
216	versions, task families, and stopping rule must be fixed through a pilot and power analysis before
217	the confirmatory evaluation.
218	
219	For compaction candidate `c` over source events `E`, measure at least:
220	
221	```text
222	source_coverage_c
223	fact_recall_c
224	contradiction_rate_c
225	task_score_c
226	input_tokens_c
227	working_context_remaining_c
228	latency_c
229	cost_c
230	sensitive_exposure_c
231	```
232	
233	No compact should be called better merely because it is shorter. It must be compared against relevant
234	baselines on task outcome, factual retention, contradiction, available working context, user control,
235	and risk.
236	
237	## Required experimental conditions
238	
239	The external reviewer should refine and preregister a factorial or blocked design that includes, at
240	minimum, these continuity modes:
241	
242	1. no supplied continuity;
243	2. human-written manual handoff;
244	3. current Carrylog checkpoint/resume envelope;
245	4. recent raw observable conversation within budget;
246	5. harness-native resume without an additional Carrylog representation;
247	6. harness-native compact, when its actual output is exposed and reusable;
248	7. a future Carrylog compact generated from the same eligible source events;
249	8. a hybrid checkpoint plus native compact;
250	9. a hybrid checkpoint plus selected raw retrieval;
251	10. a deliberately fresh project-only or no-continuity session.
252	
253	Conditions 4, 6, and 7 must not be simulated as equivalent if a provider does not expose the same
254	artifacts. An inaccessible native compact is part of the provider's hidden state and cannot be
255	silently relabeled as a portable summary.
256	
257	The design must vary:
258	
259	- same-harness resume and each supported cross-harness direction;
260	- zero, one, and repeated switch chains;
261	- short histories that fit raw, histories near the input budget, and histories that require
262	  selection or compaction;
263	- tasks dominated by facts, constraints, chronology, code state, prior errors, or user preference;
264	- helpful, irrelevant, contradictory, sensitive, and stale historical events;
265	- a native compaction before switching, where the harness exposes a detectable boundary;
266	- model version, context limit, harness version, and tool-discovery surface.
267	
268	Tasks and transitions should be randomized or counterbalanced. Evaluators should be blind to the
269	continuity condition where feasible. Ground-truth facts and scoring rubrics must be created before
270	responses are inspected. Model and harness updates require a new evidence date rather than inheriting
271	old results indefinitely.
272	
273	## Specific questions for native compaction
274	
275	The audit must answer these questions separately for each harness:
276	
277	1. Is native compaction detectable?
278	2. Is its compacted artifact visible or exportable?
279	3. Can that artifact be injected into the same harness in a fresh session?
280	4. Can it be injected into another harness without format conversion or hidden dependencies?
281	5. Does reuse outperform reconstruction from the reviewed checkpoint, selected raw events, or a new
282	   compact generated from shared sources?
283	6. Does repeated native-compaction reuse accumulate error?
284	7. Which user controls are actually available, stable, and documented?
285	
286	If a native compact is accessible, Carrylog should initially treat it as one candidate source with
287	provenance, not as canonical truth and not as an artifact that must always be reused. If it is not
288	accessible, Carrylog cannot claim to preserve it across harnesses. If raw history exceeds the target
289	budget, passing it unfiltered is not a valid baseline for routine operation; it is a stress condition
290	that must report truncation and remaining working capacity.
291	
292	## Session mode and user-intent requirements
293	
294	Any future launcher or wrapper must make continuity intent explicit. At least these modes require
295	separate evaluation:
296	
297	```text
298	resume        project state + active checkpoint + eligible prior session context
299	branch        selected checkpoint/session as a source, but a new objective and history branch
300	project-only  stable project instructions without prior task conversation
301	fresh         no Carrylog session continuity; harness behavior is explicit
302	```
303	
304	The audit should determine whether a default is safe or whether an existing session requires a
305	choice. A user must be able to see the selected mode, change it, and verify that excluded session
306	history was not injected. “Fresh” must not be advertised if repository instruction files are still
307	automatically discovered; the UI must distinguish fresh conversation from absence of project policy.
308	
309	## Record-retention questions
310	
311	The value of storing all observable records is unproven and must be tested against:
312	
313	- task success and recovery after incorrect compact or stale checkpoint;
314	- retrieval quality and latency;
315	- disk growth and operational maintenance;
316	- accidental secret, personal-data, source-code, and tool-output retention;
317	- user comprehension and willingness to enable capture;
318	- incomplete capture that creates a misleading audit trail;
319	- cross-machine and team-sharing requirements;
320	- explicit deletion, legal retention, and repository backup behavior.
321	
322	The audit should not assume “forever” as a default. It should compare checkpoint-only, bounded local
323	journal, explicit archive, and longer retention. Raw records, derived compactions, delivery packs, and
324	reviewed project memory require separate retention classes.
325	
326	If a local journal is prototyped for measurement, `.carrylog/` must be excluded without destructively
327	rewriting human ignore rules. The prototype must detect already tracked paths, nested repositories,
328	negated ignore patterns, global ignore behavior, links, permissions, and pre-existing unowned content.
329	It must fail closed instead of assuming that a `.gitignore` line prevents disclosure. No raw record
330	should enter Git or an audit bundle implicitly.
331	
332	## Threats to validity
333	
334	The reviewer must address at least these threats:
335	
336	- receipts and model self-reports can be correct parroting without behavioral use;
337	- provider system prompts, compaction, caching, and context assembly are partly hidden;
338	- model nondeterminism and upgrades can dominate small measured differences;
339	- giving evaluators the expected facts can leak answers into the task;
340	- benchmark tasks can overrepresent checkpoint-friendly work;
341	- the same model family on both sides may not represent a genuine cross-provider switch;
342	- transcript capture may be incomplete or alter user and agent behavior;
343	- longer raw context can reduce performance even when it contains every relevant fact;
344	- semantic summaries may introduce unsupported claims that structural checks cannot detect;
345	- repeated summary-of-summary evaluation can hide cumulative loss;
346	- user ratings can reward familiar UI without measuring task correctness;
347	- privacy failures may outweigh average task improvement;
348	- unavailable Cursor, Gemini, or Codex authentication can create unsupported generalization.
349	
350	## Audit work packages
351	
352	### A. Reproduce the current narrow baseline
353	
354	- Verify exact package/worktree identity and current checks.
355	- Reproduce adapter discovery evidence per harness.
356	- Reproduce the current checkpoint/resume envelope.
357	- Repeat fresh-session reconstruction across available harnesses and report unavailable cases.
358	- Separate structural success from behavioral and perceived continuity.
359	
360	### B. Design a continuity benchmark before building journaling
361	
362	- Define representative repositories, tasks, fact sets, forbidden reversals, and scoring rubrics.
363	- Establish no-context, manual-handoff, native-resume, and current Carrylog baselines.
364	- Measure one and repeated transitions with confidence intervals.
365	- Include explicit fresh/project-only user intent.
366	
367	### C. Evaluate record retention as an intervention
368	
369	- Prototype capture only to the extent required for measurement.
370	- Label complete, partial, and unavailable capture honestly.
371	- Compare checkpoint-only with bounded raw-history and retrieval conditions.
372	- Perform privacy, ignore, retention, deletion, and disk-growth review.
373	
374	### D. Evaluate compaction candidates
375	
376	- Characterize each harness-native compaction boundary and artifact accessibility.
377	- Compare native compact, Carrylog candidate, raw selection, retrieval, checkpoint, and hybrids.
378	- Measure cumulative degradation after repeated switches and repeated compaction.
379	- Require source-linked error analysis for every lost, contradicted, or invented material fact.
380	
381	### E. Review product claims and stop conditions
382	
383	- Identify claims supported now, claims requiring qualification, and claims that must be prohibited.
384	- Define evidence expiration when harness or model versions change.
385	- Recommend whether session journaling, wrapper delivery, or compaction should proceed, remain
386	  experimental, or be rejected.
387	
388	## Proposed evidence gates, subject to auditor revision
389	
390	These are gate categories, not preset numerical pass thresholds:
391	
392	1. **Delivery gate:** exact input evidence or an explicitly weaker discovery classification.
393	2. **Reconstruction gate:** preregistered relevant-fact recall and contradiction bounds.
394	3. **Behavior gate:** task non-inferiority against manual and native baselines.
395	4. **Switch-depth gate:** bounded degradation across repeated transitions.
396	5. **Compaction gate:** no material regression hidden by token reduction; adequate working context.
397	6. **Privacy gate:** capture, ignore, export, and deletion behavior withstand adversarial review.
398	7. **Intent gate:** resume, branch, project-only, and fresh behavior are distinguishable and tested.
399	8. **Perception gate:** users understand what continued and what did not.
400	
401	Thresholds must be preregistered after pilot variance is known. They must not be selected after seeing
402	which approach wins.
403	
404	## Requested external-audit output
405	
406	The reviewer should return:
407	
408	1. findings ranked by severity with direct evidence;
409	2. corrections to definitions, metrics, baselines, and experimental design;
410	3. a reproducible protocol and required harness access;
411	4. a claim-by-claim matrix of proven, partially supported, unproven, and unfalsifiable statements;
412	5. privacy and retention findings independent of continuity performance;
413	6. a recommendation for current checkpoint/resume claims;
414	7. a separate recommendation for session journaling;
415	8. a separate recommendation for Carrylog compaction;
416	9. explicit NO-GO conditions and evidence-expiration rules.
417	
418	The audit must not return one undifferentiated product GO. Structural checkpoint safety, cross-harness
419	delivery, behavioral continuity, journaling value, and compaction value are separate decisions.
420	
421	## Interim product constraint
422	
423	Until this audit protocol is reviewed and a baseline experiment is completed:
424	
425	- do not claim that Carrylog resumes conversations;
426	- do not claim that arbitrary or repeated harness switching preserves effective context;
427	- do not claim that all-record retention is beneficial;
428	- do not claim that a Carrylog compact is superior to native compact;
429	- do not implement automatic semantic compaction as a default;
430	- do not treat a continuity receipt as proof of behavioral use;
431	- keep the accepted 0.1 boundary limited to reviewed project checkpoint and resume-envelope recovery.
432	
433	Research prototypes must remain clearly labeled, local-first, reversible, and outside the stable
434	runtime contract until the relevant evidence gate passes.

9	## Scope
10

13	parser, or Carrylog compactor.
14	
15	## Experimental matrix
16	
17	```text
18	repositories: 2
19	tasks per repository: 5
20	conditions: no-context, manual-handoff, carrylog-resume
21	harnesses: 2 authenticated harnesses from different supported surfaces
22	planned runs: 2 * 5 * 3 * 2 = 60
23	```
24	
25	Repository R1 may be Carrylog. R2 must differ materially in stack, size, ownership history, and task
26	shape. The exact commits or immutable fixture digests must be recorded before execution.
27	
28	The two harnesses should initially be Codex and Claude Code because they use distinct instruction and
29	Skill surfaces. If either is unavailable, substitution requires a committed protocol amendment before
30	results are generated.
31	
32	## Task families
33	
34	Each repository contributes one task from each family:
35	
36	1. reconstruct the current objective and safest next action;
37	2. continue a bounded implementation without repeating completed work;
38	3. preserve a protected architecture or compatibility decision;
39	4. avoid a previously failed approach and explain the relevant risk;
40	5. diagnose or verify state using the repository's required commands and limits.
41	
42	Every task fixture must define before execution:
43	
44	- relevant facts with fixed importance weights;
45	- prohibited reversals and repeated-work indicators;
46	- allowed clarification questions;
47	- expected verification behavior;
48	- a task-specific scoring rubric;
49	- sensitive facts that must not appear in output.
50	
51	## Conditions
52	
53	### No context
54	
55	Start the harness in the repository without a manual handoff or Carrylog resume envelope. Record any
56	project instructions the harness discovers automatically; this condition is not necessarily absence
57	of repository policy.
58	
59	### Manual handoff
60	
61	Provide a concise maintainer-written handoff that fits the same factual rubric. Freeze its exact bytes
62	before execution.
63	
64	### Carrylog resume
65	
66	Use the current validated checkpoint/resume workflow without adding an experimental journal or
67	semantic summary. Record artifact digests, discovery evidence, and any delivery evidence the harness
68	actually exposes.
69	
70	## Measures
71	
72	Report separately:
73	
74	- weighted relevant-fact reconstruction recall;
75	- weighted contradiction rate;
76	- prohibited reversal count;
77	- repeated-work count;
78	- unnecessary clarification count;
79	- task completion score under the preregistered rubric;
80	- input context size where observable;
81	- latency and estimated cost;
82	- evaluator confidence and unavailable evidence.
83	
84	Do not create a post-hoc composite utility score. Receipts and acknowledgements are delivery or
85	self-report evidence, not behavioral success.
86	
87	## Execution controls
88	
89	- Commit this protocol, task fixtures, rubrics, prompts, order-generation seed, and analysis script
90	  before the first scored run.
91	- Randomize or counterbalance condition and harness order within each task.
92	- Use fresh sessions and disable accidental conversation reuse.
93	- Record model and harness versions, context settings, repository commit, Carrylog commit, start time,
94	  exit status, and unavailable tools.
95	- Preserve sanitized raw visible output. Never collect hidden reasoning, credentials, or private
96	  provider stores.
97	- Score blind to condition where practical; record when blinding is impossible.
98	- Do not replace failed runs silently. Keep exclusions and reasons.

100	## Pilot interpretation
101	
102	Tier 1 estimates variance and exposes failure modes. It does not authorize a claim of universal
103	conversation resume, arbitrary switch invariance, journaling value, or compaction superiority.

105	Proceed to a larger independent Tier 2 design only when Carrylog resume shows a consistent beneficial
106	direction over no-context and no material unexplained regression against manual handoff. Exact
107	non-inferiority margins and sample sizes must be chosen from pilot variance before Tier 2, not after
108	inspecting confirmatory results.
109	
110	If the pilot shows no useful signal, stop continuity expansion and investigate whether the product's
111	value is governance, reviewability, or deterministic checkpoint safety rather than behavioral resume.

113	## Required outputs

120	  prompts/

126	```

1	# ADR-0012: Require evidence gates before expanding continuity claims
2	
3	- Status: Accepted
4	- Date: 2026-07-12
5	- Owners: Repository maintainer
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	ADR-0010 deliberately limits Carrylog continuity to reviewed repository state plus fresh Git
10	evidence. Later discussion considered visible delivery receipts, observable session journals,
11	cross-harness launch wrappers, and reversible compaction. Those ideas could improve the experience,
12	but the project has not demonstrated that arbitrary harness switching preserves effective context,
13	that retaining all observable conversation improves outcomes, or that Carrylog compaction would
14	outperform harness-native resume or compaction.
15	
16	The initial audit brief proposed a comprehensive factorial evaluation. External review agreed with
17	its evidence discipline but found the first execution plan too large for a solo beta. Waiting for a
18	full research program would leave the project in a permanent pre-release state; implementing the
19	features first would turn unproven assumptions into product contracts.
20	
21	## Decision
22	
23	Carrylog retains the accepted ADR-0010 boundary. It is a repository-owned project-memory governance
24	and checkpoint tool, not a conversation-replay product.
25	
26	Continuity evidence is classified in increasing strength:
27	
28	1. **artifact:** the expected repository state exists and is current;
29	2. **delivery:** the intended state is demonstrably included in model-visible input;
30	3. **reconstruction:** the model recovers preregistered relevant facts and constraints;
31	4. **behavior:** the next task preserves decisions, avoids repeated work, and uses prior state;
32	5. **perception:** the user correctly understands what continued and experiences useful continuity.
33	
34	Evidence at one level does not prove the next. A generated file, discovery trace, receipt, or model
35	acknowledgement is not behavioral continuity.
36	
37	Before session journaling or semantic compaction becomes a supported runtime feature or enabled
38	default, the project must run a minimum viable Tier 1 pilot:
39	
40	- two materially different repositories;
41	- five continuation tasks per repository;
42	- no-context, manual-handoff, and current Carrylog checkpoint conditions;
43	- two authenticated harnesses;
44	- prompts, facts, prohibited reversals, rubrics, and analysis rules committed before execution;
45	- sanitized raw results and all exclusions retained for review.
46	
47	Tier 1 is an exploratory maintainer-run pilot, not external proof. It estimates variance, exposes
48	harness problems, and decides whether larger work is justified. An independent Tier 2 evaluation is
49	required before broad behavioral or compaction superiority claims.
50	
51	Research may prototype the minimum capture or delivery mechanism required to measure a hypothesis,
52	but prototypes stay outside the stable runtime contract. Carrylog must not default to automatic
53	semantic compaction, indefinite conversation retention, or raw transcript export before the
54	applicable evidence and privacy gates pass.
55	
56	Native resume and native compact are baselines, not obstacles to replace. If a harness exposes a
57	native compact artifact, an experiment may reuse it with provenance. An inaccessible native compact
58	cannot be described as portable or reconstructed. Carrylog compact, selected raw history, retrieval,
59	and hybrid approaches must be compared on factual retention, contradictions, task outcome, working
60	context, cost, latency, and exposure—not token reduction alone.
61	
62	Future session UX must distinguish at least `resume`, `branch`, `project-only`, and `fresh` intent.
63	Repository instruction discovery may still occur during a fresh conversation, so the product must
64	not equate fresh conversation with absence of project policy.
65	
66	The narrow checkpoint/resume beta is not blocked on proving every future continuity hypothesis. A
67	known research gap is documented and the beta may ship when its current claims, package, security,
68	review, and release gates pass. High-severity integrity or data-loss findings remain release blockers;
69	evidence work is not a reason to ignore them.
70	
71	Every new continuity feature must trace to a job in `docs/product-scope.md`. “More sophisticated” or
72	“more defensive” is not independently a product job.
73	
74	## Considered alternatives
75	
76	### Implement journaling and compaction before measurement
77	
78	Rejected. It would create retention, privacy, and compatibility contracts before demonstrating user
79	value.
80	
81	### Require the complete factorial audit before beta publication
82	
83	Rejected. The cost is disproportionate to the current narrow product claim and would prevent the
84	project from obtaining the users needed for meaningful evidence.
85	
86	### Treat a continuity receipt as proof
87	
88	Rejected. A receipt can attest attempted delivery and model acknowledgement but not correct use.
89	
90	### Reuse every harness-native compact automatically
91	
92	Rejected. Availability, format, hidden dependencies, and cross-harness value differ and require
93	per-harness evidence.
94	
95	### Market Carrylog as universal conversation resume
96	
97	Rejected until behavioral and perceived-continuity evidence supports that claim. The defensible
98	current position is Git-reviewable, tool-neutral project memory and checkpoint governance.
99	
100	## Consequences
101	
102	Positive:
103	
104	- the current beta can ship without pretending a research roadmap is already proven;
105	- small public experiments replace indefinite audit planning;
106	- receipts, journals, and compaction receive claim-specific gates;
107	- native harness behavior remains a measured baseline;
108	- future session designs must preserve explicit fresh and branch choices.
109	
110	Negative:
111	
112	- Carrylog cannot yet promise conversation continuity or arbitrary switch invariance;
113	- authenticated harness access and experimental execution are required before expansion;
114	- research artifacts need privacy review and may reveal that proposed features are not worthwhile;
115	- model and harness updates can expire earlier results.
116	
117	## Validation and evidence expiration
118	
119	- Execute the committed Tier 1 protocol under `research/continuity/` before promoting research
120	  journaling or compaction into the supported runtime.
121	- Report unavailable delivery evidence as unknown, not successful.
122	- Preserve model, harness, context-limit, prompt, repository, and commit identities with results.
123	- Re-run affected evidence when an instruction-discovery surface, model generation, native compact
124	  policy, or wrapper delivery path materially changes.
125	- Revisit this ADR if Tier 1 shows no useful signal, external users identify a different primary job,
126	  or a broadly adopted standard provides stronger portable continuity primitives.

1	# Product scope
2	
3	## Product statement
4	
5	Carrylog is a local-first project-context governance and handoff layer for teams and individual
6	developers who switch among AI coding agents. It gives a repository one canonical, reviewable,
7	versioned context source and compiles small adapters for each supported tool. It preserves durable
8	project truth rather than capturing or reconstructing private session transcripts.
9	
10	## Primary users
11	
12	1. Developers who use Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, or similar tools on the same codebase.
13	2. Teams that need agent changes to follow shared architecture, quality, and handoff constraints.
14	3. Maintainers who want context changes reviewed through normal Git workflows.
15	
16	## Jobs to be done
17	
18	- Continue work in a new agent without manually retelling the project state.
19	- Know whether project context is missing, stale, oversized, or inconsistent with generated files.
20	- Add a new agent adapter without creating another independently maintained project memory.
21	- Leave a verifiable handoff that distinguishes facts, checks, assumptions, and unresolved risk.
22	- Keep context loading proportional to the task instead of injecting every document every time.
23	
24	## Product invariants
25	
26	- Canonical human-authored state is separate from generated adapters.
27	- Default commands do not delete or silently replace pre-existing human content.
28	- Read and write paths remain inside the project and do not traverse symlinks.
29	- Core behavior is deterministic, offline-capable, and inspectable.
30	- A failed preflight does not partially update another adapter.
31	- Context freshness is never claimed without evidence.
32	
33	## Explicit non-goals
34	
35	- Replacing project management, source control, ADR systems, or documentation platforms.
36	- Prescribing PRD-to-implementation workflows like a complete agent methodology.
37	- Automatically deciding architecture or product priorities.
38	- Hiding an LLM call behind validation or deterministic commands.
39	- Treating token count alone as context quality.
40	- Reproducing a coding agent's hidden session state, full conversation, or internal compaction
41	  behavior; continuity is based on explicit, reviewable project and task checkpoints.
42	- Replacing hook- or daemon-based automatic session journals; those can consume exported repository
43	  context later without becoming part of the deterministic core.
44	- Supporting every agent through guessed formats; each adapter needs a researched and tested
45	  conformance contract.
46	
47	## Success measures
48	
49	The technical beta is successful when it is safe and predictable across dogfood and representative
50	adoption fixtures. External beta learning and the stable gate add measurable product outcomes:
51	
52	- reduced manual onboarding text when switching agents;
53	- zero unmanaged-content loss in adoption and synchronization tests;
54	- deterministic adapter output across supported operating systems;
55	- bounded always-loaded context with transparent measurement;
56	- handoffs that another agent can continue from without asking for basic state reconstruction;
57	- migration guarantees for every published configuration version.
58	
59	Exact telemetry is intentionally not collected by the local CLI in the current scope. Any future
60	analytics must be opt-in and must not upload repository content.
61	
62	These outcome measures are targets, not current results. Structural adapter, checkpoint, and package
63	tests do not prove behavioral or perceived continuity. ADR-0012 requires a staged Tier 1 pilot before
64	the product expands into session journaling, semantic compaction, or broader continuity claims.
65	
66	New features must trace to one of the jobs above or update this scope through an explicit product
67	decision. Additional sophistication or defensive depth is not a user job by itself.

227	
228	Applies recognized exact-template context migrations, recompiles adapter blocks, and repairs a missing

234	carrylog sync --dry-run     # show the plan without writing

239	identity, physical containment, and expected content are rechecked during commit. Individual
240	replacements are atomic on supported local filesystems, and stale plans are rejected if a file or
241	loaded configuration changed after inspection. Sequential multi-file rename is not claimed to be an
242	OS-level transaction; portable path-based syscalls still have the residual race documented in the

337	## Design and safety commitments
338	
339	- **Local-first:** normal runtime makes no network or model calls.
340	- **Progressive disclosure:** routers instruct agents to read selected documents first and defer
341	  task-specific references until needed.
342	- **Non-destructive adoption:** existing unmarked instruction files require explicit review/adoption.
343	- **Deterministic output:** rendered bodies are deterministic for the same validated config and
344	  inspected Git state; managed-file newlines and surrounding human content are preserved inputs.
345	- **Exclusive ownership:** config, schema, documents, and adapters cannot share normalized paths.
346	- **Fail closed:** malformed config/markers, path escape, symlinks, drift, and budget violations fail.
347	- **Bounded Git:** sanitized environment, disabled fsmonitor, no shell, deadline, output ceiling,
348	  stable repeated observations, and lossless safely escaped unusual-filename representation.
349	- **No telemetry:** repository context is not uploaded by the core CLI.
350	- **Portable, not private-session replay:** checkpoint/resume reconstructs reviewed project state;
351	  provider-native transcripts and compaction remain outside Carrylog's boundary.
352	
353	The beta intentionally does not claim semantic code-to-document freshness, exact tokenizer counts,
354	cross-filesystem transactions, or support for agents whose discovery behavior has not been researched.
355	See the [threat model](docs/threat-model.md) for residual risks.

1	# Adapter compatibility
2	
3	Adapter support is based on documented instruction discovery, not filename guesses. Sources were
4	rechecked on 2026-07-11. Carrylog models instruction *surfaces*, not one output per harness: Codex and
5	Cursor share `AGENTS.md` ownership.
6	
7	| Adapter | Default output | Supported beta contract | Official behavior source |
8	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
9	| Codex | `AGENTS.md` | Root managed block that routes to canonical context | [Custom instructions with AGENTS.md](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md.md) |
10	| Claude Code | `CLAUDE.md` | Root managed block that routes to canonical context | [How Claude remembers your project](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) |
11	| Cursor | `AGENTS.md` | Shared `agents` surface with Codex | [Cursor rules](https://cursor.com/docs/rules) |
12	| Gemini CLI | `GEMINI.md` | Root router and generic workspace Skill discovery | [GEMINI.md](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/gemini-md/) and [Agent Skills](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/) |
13	
14	## Codex
15	
16	Codex builds guidance once per run/session. It reads global guidance, then walks from the project
17	root to the working directory. At each level it prefers `AGENTS.override.md`, then `AGENTS.md`, then
18	configured fallbacks; nearer files appear later and override broader guidance. The default combined
19	project-document limit is 32 KiB.
20	
21	The beta adapter owns a block in the configured output, defaulting to the repository-root
22	`AGENTS.md`. It does not automatically generate a nested hierarchy, overrides, fallback
23	configuration, or global guidance. A custom nested output is written when configured, but discovery
24	and conformance for that path are user-owned. Existing human content is preserved through explicit
25	adoption.
26	
27	Codex project prompt inspection on 2026-07-11 discovered both the generated root `AGENTS.md` and the
28	generic `.agents/skills/carrylog-continuity/SKILL.md` without invoking a model.
29	
30	## Claude Code
31	
32	Claude Code loads `CLAUDE.md`/`CLAUDE.local.md` files above the working directory at launch and loads
33	subdirectory instructions when it works there. A project file can live at `./CLAUDE.md` or
34	`./.claude/CLAUDE.md`; concise files under roughly 200 lines are recommended.
35	
36	The beta adapter defaults to `./CLAUDE.md`. It does not automatically generate `.claude/rules/`,
37	local personal instructions, imports, exclusions, or organization policy. A custom nested output is
38	written when configured, but discovery and conformance for that path are user-owned.
39	
40	When Skills are enabled, Carrylog writes a minimal `.claude/skills/carrylog-continuity/SKILL.md`
41	adapter that directs Claude Code to the canonical generic Skill. Both Skill folders pass the
42	frontmatter validator from the Codex Skill creator. Claude Code 2.1.207 is installed locally; a fresh
43	authenticated read-only session reconstructed the v2 project, objective, next action, stale status,
44	and risks from Carrylog resume output.
45	
46	## Cursor
47	
48	Cursor supports `AGENTS.md` as a project-rules surface. Configuration v2 therefore maps both `codex`
49	and `cursor` harness selection to one `agents` adapter and one default `AGENTS.md`, preventing
50	duplicate ownership. Carrylog does not generate Cursor legacy `.cursorrules` or project `.mdc` rules.
51	
52	Cursor CLI is not installed in the current validation environment. File discovery is covered by the
53	official contract and exact shared-surface fixture; authenticated fresh-session launch remains an
54	explicit gap rather than a claimed result.
55	
56	## Gemini CLI
57	
58	Gemini CLI loads hierarchical `GEMINI.md` context and supports workspace Skills from
59	`.gemini/skills` or the generic `.agents/skills` alias. Carrylog generates the root `GEMINI.md` router
60	and reuses the generic Skill instead of duplicating it under `.gemini`.
61	
62	Local Gemini CLI discovery on 2026-07-11 reported `carrylog-continuity` enabled from the generated
63	`.agents/skills` path. Carrylog does not generate custom context filenames, nested GEMINI files, or
64	extensions. A headless model launch could not authenticate without an interactive login or API key,
65	so discovery—not authenticated response quality—is the verified Gemini boundary in this environment.
66	
67	## Guarantees and limits
68	
69	- The registry is the single runtime source for adapter labels and default outputs.
70	- Golden fixtures freeze exact managed-block output for v1 Codex/Claude and v2 agents/Gemini
71	  surfaces.
72	- Default routers contain references and load policy, not full canonical document bodies.
73	- A custom output path is accepted when portable, but the user is responsible for choosing a path
74	  the target tool discovers.
75	- CI does not require authenticated model launches; conformance covers documented discovery, exact
76	  output, adoption, drift, cross-platform file behavior, and offline local discovery where available.
77	
78	Copilot, overrides, and nested generation remain unsupported until each has a documented discovery,
79	precedence, ownership, and fixture contract.

1	# Threat model
2	
3	## Assets
4	
5	- Human-authored project instructions and context.
6	- Repository integrity and content outside generated blocks.
7	- Files outside the repository.
8	- Confidential information present in project documents.
9	- Portable resume-envelope confidentiality and integrity.
10	- CI reliability and machine-readable diagnostics.
11	
12	## Trust boundaries
13	
14	The user intentionally runs `carrylog` in a repository. The repository, configuration, Markdown,
15	existing adapter files, path names, and symlinks are inputs and may be malformed or malicious.
16	Node.js, the local operating system, and the installed package are trusted within the normal CLI
17	execution model.
18	
19	The current runtime does not make network calls or invoke a model. Package installation still has
20	the normal npm supply-chain boundary.
21	
22	## Addressed threats
23	
24	| Threat | Current control |
25	| --- | --- |
26	| `../` or absolute-path writes | Portable relative-path validation plus root containment check |
27	| Symlink or parent-substitution write escape | Reject links; guard existing directory device/inode identity; recheck physical containment and parent identity before staging and rename |
28	| Windows-specific path aliasing | Reserved-name/character validation and normalized separators |
29	| Case or Unicode path collision | Conservative NFKC plus multi-step case-normalized comparison |
30	| YAML duplicate keys or alias expansion | Strict parsing, unique keys, bounded alias expansion |
31	| Existing instruction loss | Refuse unmarked files unless `--adopt`; replace only marked content |
32	| Partial update after another adapter is invalid | Plan and validate all adapters before writing |
33	| Torn individual file | Sibling temporary file and rename |
34	| Prompt-router marker injection through metadata | Single-line bounded metadata and reserved-marker rejection |
35	| Oversized startup context | Configured hard budget over actual always-loaded characters |
36	| Oversized/binary config or context | Bounded reads, catalog limits, router budget, strict UTF-8 |
37	| Aggregate on-demand context exhaustion during resume | 8 MiB total configuration/document observation budget before a second observation is retained |
38	| Generated/source path alias | One conservative compatibility/case-normalized ownership graph including copied schema |
39	| Concurrent human edit or stale loaded config | Exact bounded config re-read at command entry plus expected-content checks before each remaining rename |
40	| Git repository redirection | Remove inherited repository-selection `GIT_*` variables |
41	| Git fsmonitor code execution | Force `core.fsmonitor=false` on every Git subcommand |
42	| Git process/resource abuse | No shell, no prompts, deadline with KILL escalation, combined 1 MiB output |
43	| Malicious Git filenames, subjects, or repository Markdown | NUL-delimited Buffer parsing, reversible invalid-UTF-8 hex, HTML-aware checkpoint structure, and terminal-safe human/JSON output while preserving parsed JSON values |
44	| Mixed-time Git evidence | Two observations matching allowed exit codes and exact stdout per attempt, three bounded retries, then fail closed |
45	| Handoff context inflation | 200-path rendering cap plus prospective file/context-budget validation |
46	| Resume path substitution, linked export, or same-size overwrite with restored mtime | Guarded handle/path checks over device, inode, size, mtime, ctime, and link count plus symlink and hard-link rejection |
47	| Mixed-time resume envelope | Config/documents → stable Git → config/documents observation with three bounded retries and exact-byte revalidation |
48	| Private-session leakage | Resume excludes transcripts, hidden reasoning, provider stores, absolute roots, session IDs, and commit timestamps |
49	| Generated Skill overwrite | Exactly one standalone ownership marker; no adoption or merge of unowned Skill files |
50	
51	## Residual risks
52	
53	- Multi-file writes stage all temporary content before rename, but sequential commit is not atomic
54	  across process termination, filesystem faults, or races during rename.
55	- A repository owner can intentionally place harmful instructions in canonical Markdown; this tool
56	  validates structure, not truth or intent.
57	- Normal validation and replacement do not reject every hard-linked source. Replacement-by-rename
58	  does not mutate the linked inode, but non-export reads can still observe linked content. The
59	  confidentiality-sensitive `resume` export rejects any canonical config or document with link count
60	  greater than one.
61	- Parent/content/temporary identity checks narrow but do not eliminate the TOCTOU interval between a
62	  final check and path-based `mkdir`, temporary creation, or rename. Portable Node APIs do not expose
63	  directory-descriptor `openat`/`renameat` or atomic compare-and-swap replacement. A detected swap
64	  prevents managed content commit, but a raced path-based `mkdir` can have an external directory side
65	  effect before its postcondition fails.
66	- Character count is not a tokenizer and cannot predict every model's context cost.
67	- npm lifecycle and dependency compromise are outside runtime path controls. The project currently
68	  uses one runtime dependency and a committed lockfile to reduce exposure.
69	- JSON diagnostics may contain local paths and parser excerpts; CI log handling remains the caller's
70	  responsibility.
71	- Agents can still place inaccurate or sensitive prose into reviewed checkpoint sections. Carrylog
72	  validates structure and file identity, not semantic truth or secret classification.
73	
74	## Security principles for future features
75	
76	- Git inspection must retain direct argument arrays, sanitized environment, disabled executable
77	  config, combined output limits, timeouts, and no shell.
78	- Handoff generation must never stage or commit files automatically.
79	- Compaction must keep recoverable history and must not overwrite source material without explicit
80	  review.
81	- Session journaling, persistent conversation capture, and semantic compaction require a separate data
82	  retention and privacy threat model before entering the supported runtime.
83	- MCP mutation tools must be opt-in, narrowly scoped, and distinguish reads from writes.
84	- Remote services and telemetry require a separate threat model and explicit consent.
85	- Plugin and skill installation must not execute unreviewed scripts implicitly.
86	
87	## Security test backlog
88	
89	- Additional hard-link and reparse-point behavior on supported Windows filesystems.
90	- Deterministic injection at the exact rename/permission syscalls beyond behavioral fault fixtures.
91	- Very deep paths, long filenames, large YAML, and large Markdown limits.
92	- Additional Windows reparse-point variants beyond the directory-junction regression.
93	- Submodule helper execution and additional executable Git configuration beyond fsmonitor.
